episodes.165592: Periods of moderate to heavy rain occurred on February 17th into the 18th in response to a passing cold front. Southeast Ohio took the brunt of precipitation, resulting in 1 to 2 inches of rainfall accumulations. Many state roads in this portion of the state were forced to close due to the deluge of water along the roadways and were closed for over 24 hours. The rain concluded on the 18th as the cold front completed its passage, but flooding issues extended into the next days as many of the mainstem rivers rose out of their banks and inflicted minor flooding in areas adjacent to the river.
episodes.165621: As an upper trough persisted over the island chain, heavy showers developed over the Big Island and Maui on different days.  The precipitation produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.165817: Several rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms moved across the region on the 17th. Two to four inches were common, which resulted in isolated flash flooding and more widespread flooding of rivers. The heavy rain occurred ahead of a cold front as it entered southeast Missouri and southern Illinois from the northwest. Weak waves of low pressure moved northeast along the front. A strong 850 mb jet up to 60 to 70 knots was accompanied by a strong surge of warm moist air through the Mississippi River Valley.
episodes.165818: Several rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms moved across the region on the 17th. Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches created pockets of road flooding and then widespread river flooding in subsequent days. The heavy rain occurred ahead of a cold front as it entered southeast Missouri and southern Illinois from the northwest. Weak waves of low pressure moved northeast along the front. A strong 850 mb jet up to 60 to 70 knots was accompanied by a strong surge of warm moist air through the Mississippi River Valley.
episodes.166282: Heavy rain brought flooding to several rivers in northeast Arkansas in mid February.
episodes.166771: A Clipper low pressure system moving through the Upper Great Lakes brought storm force northwest winds to east half portions of Lake Superior from late on the 18th into the morning of the 19th.
episodes.166772: A Clipper low pressure system moving through the Upper Great Lakes produced storm force northwest wind gusts at Minneapolis Shoal Light on the evening of the 18th.

The Belleville Lock of the Ohio River observed the river rising out of its 35 foot flood stage on the morning of February 19th. The river crested at 36.53 feet just before sunrise on the 20th and returned to its banks that evening. While this portion of the Ohio River was in flood, Ohio State Route 124, which resides adjacent to the river up to the Meigs/Washington County line, flooded as well as smaller roads that feed into Route 124.

Moderate flooding occurred on the Little Wabash River. At the Carmi river gage, the river crested at 32.94 feet on the evening of the 27th. Flood stage is 27 feet. There was considerable flooding of low-lying farmland and fields. Some rural back country roads were under water. The river remained above flood stage into March.

The Hocking River at Athens rose out of its 20 foot flood stage late in the afternoon on February 19th. The river remained above its flood stage for only a brief period of time and was back in its banks that evening. Low lying areas around the river and the nearby campground observed minor flooding between Athens and Coolville while the Hocking River was out of its banks.

Moderate flooding occurred on the Wabash River. At Mount Carmel, the river crested at 26.4 feet on the 28th. Flood stage is 19 feet. Some farm operations were affected, such as moving equipment to higher ground. Extensive lowland flooding occurred, affecting numerous local river roads.  Installation of flood gate A at Mount Carmel was necessary.  County Road 1280 E and South Division Street were flooded. The flooding continued into March.
The Wabash River rose above flood stage and remained there into March. The crest did not occur until March.
